title: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
subtitle: DLBCL NOS · HGBCL with MYC + BCL2 rearrangements · PMBL · transformed · HIV-associated. ~60–70% are cured with first-line R-CHOP-based therapy — the questions are double-hit status, IPI, CNS risk, fitness for anthracycline, and at relapse, timing (<12 vs ≥12 months) and CAR-T eligibility
source: Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin (Chou L, Schroers-Martin J, Gupta NK) and HIV-associated lymphoma · NCCN · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026.

blocks.heading: What the pathologist has to tell you
rows: GCB = CD10+, or CD10− BCL6+ MUM1−. Everything else is non-GCB (ABC-like) — worse on R-CHOP, and the group where Pola-R-CHP gained most. GEP is more accurate than IHC

MYC-rearranged in ~10% of aggressive B-NHL, half with BCL2. MYC + BCL2 rearranged = HGBCL / DLBCL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (formerly “double hit”). WHO-HAEM5 folds MYC + BCL6 back into DLBCL NOS / HGBL NOS; ICC keeps it provisional
MYC ≥40% + BCL2 ≥50% protein without rearrangement — ~20–25%, intermediate prognosis, treated as DLBCL NOS. Not the same as double hit
CD30 → BV option at relapse · EBV+ DLBCL (any age, worse) · CD5+ enriched for CNS relapse

blocks.heading: Workup
items: Excisional or core biopsy — never FNA; hematopathology review
PET/CT (staging + Deauville response); marrow biopsy only if it changes management — PET detects most marrow disease
Labs: CBC, CMP, LDH, uric acid; HBsAg + anti-HBc, HCV, HIV
Echo or MUGA before anthracycline · fertility counselling · pregnancy test
LP (cytology + flow) if CNS-IPI high or high-risk site; MRI brain if symptomatic

blocks.heading: IPI — APLES: age >60 · PS ≥2 · LDH ↑ · ≥2 extranodal · stage III–IV
blocks.footnote: Shipp NEJM 1993 · Ziepert JCO 2010. CNS-IPI = IPI + kidney/adrenal (0–6): 2-yr CNS relapse 0–1: 0.6% · 2–3: 3.4% · 4–6: 10.2% (Schmitz JCO 2016).

boxes: FLYER: age ≤60, aaIPI 0, <7.5 cm → 4 R-CHOP + 2 R
S1001: R-CHOP ×3 → iPET; neg → 1 more (no RT)
bulky or IPI-risk → treat as advanced
still no significant OS gain at 5 yr
PMBL: DA-EPOCH-R, or R-CHOP ± RT (see p2)
no maintenance, no consolidative ASCT in CR
do a geriatric assessment, prephase prednisone
bridge with R-chemo, pola, or RT
salvage R-ICE / R-DHAP / R-GDP → ASCT if CMR/PR
CAR-T is also reasonable — data are from <12 mo

blocks.heading: Limited stage — the evidence
items: FLYER: 4 R-CHOP + 2 rituximab non-inferior to 6 R-CHOP — 3-yr PFS 96% vs 93%, a third less toxicity. Only for age 18–60, aaIPI 0, bulk <7.5 cm
SWOG S1001 (single-arm phase 2): R-CHOP ×3 → interim PET; 89% were PET-negative and got just 1 more cycle, no RT. 5-yr PFS 87%, OS 89%; iPET-positive patients (RT) did as well
SWOG 8736 (CHOP ×3 + RT beat CHOP ×8) is pre-rituximab, and its advantage vanished on long follow-up. RT now: bulk, PET-positive residual, or when chemo must be short

blocks.heading: Advanced stage — the evidence
items: R-CHOP is 20+ years old (GELA LNH-98.5: 10-yr OS 43.5% vs 27.6% over CHOP). Many add-ons failed: ibrutinib (PHOENIX), obinutuzumab (GOYA), venetoclax (CAVALLI), R-CHOP vs DA-EPOCH-R (CALGB 50303)

POLARIX (Pola-R-CHP): 2-yr PFS 76.7% vs 70.2%, HR 0.73. 5-yr update: PFS HR 0.77 (64.9% vs 59.1%), OS HR 0.85 — not significant. Benefit concentrated in ABC/non-GCB, IPI 3–5, age >60. Needs G-CSF. Standard option for IPI ≥2

frontMIND (tafasitamab + lenalidomide + R-CHOP, IPI 3–5): PFS HR 0.75, 2-yr 71.1% vs 62.9%; OS immature (HR 0.85). More grade ≥3 AEs (87% vs 76%) and fatal AEs (6% vs 4%). Not FDA-approved — sBLA filed 2026

blocks.heading: CNS prophylaxis — the case against HD-MTX
items: Who is high risk: CNS-IPI 4–6 · kidney/adrenal · testicular · breast, uterine · epidural / paranasal / skull base · HGBCL MYC+BCL2

HD-MTX does not clearly prevent CNS relapse. 1,923 ultra-high-risk patients (Wilson JCO 2026): 3-yr CNS relapse 8.1% with vs 9.3% without HD-MTX, adjusted HR 1.13 — no benefit in any subgroup. Alberta cohort: 11.2% vs 12.2%
End-of-treatment timing is no worse than intercalated (5.8% vs 5.7%) and avoids R-CHOP delays. Adding IT did not lower CNS relapse
Practical: image/LP high-risk patients at diagnosis; testicular DLBCL still gets CNS-directed therapy + contralateral testis RT; otherwise HD-MTX 3–3.5 g/m² ×2–4 is a shared-decision, not a default

blocks.heading: Staging — Cotswolds-modified Ann Arbor
rows: One lymph node region or lymphoid structure (spleen, thymus, Waldeyer ring)
≥2 regions, same side of the diaphragm. Hilar nodes are lateralized — bilateral involvement is stage II
Regions on both sides of the diaphragm
Disseminated — marrow, CNS, or more than one extranodal site
B = weight loss >10% over 6 mo, or unexplained fever >38°C in the past month, or recurrent drenching night sweats
S splenic · X bulky: node ≥10 cm, or mediastinal mass ≥⅓ the transverse thoracic diameter at T5–6 · E limited direct extranodal extension
blocks.footnote: A single extranodal site as the only disease is IE; more than one extranodal site is stage IV. Hilar (bronchopulmonary) nodes sit outside the mediastinum.

pages.subtitle: Page 2 — high-grade and mediastinal variants, special populations, and relapsed / refractory disease

blocks.heading: HGBCL with MYC + BCL2 rearrangements
items: FISH every new DLBCL — morphology and COO do not predict it. Often high LDH, marrow and CNS involvement

DA-EPOCH-R ×6 is the usual choice (single-arm, MYC-rearranged: 4-yr EFS 71%, OS 77%; Dunleavy 2018) — no randomized proof it beats R-CHOP; Pola-R-CHP is used by some (small POLARIX subset). Evaluate the CNS at diagnosis
No consolidative ASCT in first CR. Relapse → CAR-T

blocks.heading: Primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma (PMBL)
rows: Young (median ~30s), women, bulky anterior mediastinal mass ± SVC syndrome. Biology overlaps nodular-sclerosis cHL: 9p24.1 amplification → PD-L1/PD-L2; CD30 often weakly +
NCI phase 2 (n=51): EFS 93%, OS 97% at 5 yr; only 2 of 51 needed RT. Avoids mediastinal RT (breast cancer, cardiac disease) in young women
Accepted alternative. IELSG37: if end-of-chemo PET is CMR (Deauville 1–3), omit RT — 30-mo PFS 96.2% observation vs 98.5% RT, 5-yr OS 99% both. Deauville 5 does poorly (5-yr PFS 60%)

Pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-170: ORR 45%, CR 13%; accelerated approval) · nivolumab + BV (CheckMate 436: ORR 73%, CR 37%; not FDA-approved for PMBL) · CAR-T (included in LBCL labels) · salvage + ASCT if chemosensitive
blocks.footnote: Mediastinal gray-zone lymphoma (PMBL/cHL features, often CD15+, CD20 variable): worse than either; DA-EPOCH-R, ISRT if localized.

blocks.heading: HIV-associated aggressive B-cell lymphoma
rows: Continue or start ART through chemotherapy (check interactions — avoid boosted PIs/cobicistat with vincristine). PJP (TMP-SMX), MAC prophylaxis if CD4 <100, fluconazole, acyclovir; consider quinolone at nadir if CD4 <100

R-CHOP or DA-EPOCH-R ×6 (with ART, outcomes approach HIV-negative). AMC-034: concurrent R-EPOCH CR 73% vs sequential 55%. Rituximab caveat: CD4 <50 — AMC-010 infectious deaths 14% vs 2% (60% of them at CD4 <50)
CD20−, CD138+, MUM1+, EBV+ in most, MYC often rearranged; oral cavity. Rituximab useless — DA-EPOCH (± bortezomib, small series); poor outcomes
HHV8+ (most EBV+), effusions without a mass, CD20−, CD30+, CD138+. Modified EPOCH (NCI: median OS 22 mo); IL-6 high = worse. Exclude KSHV-MCD/KS
IT MTX for marrow, paranasal sinus, testicular or epidural involvement (handbook): 12 mg d1+5 of cycles 3–5, or weekly ×4 in cycle 1

blocks.heading: Relapsed / refractory DLBCL — agents, evidence, status (Sept 2026)
rows: ZUMA-7 vs salvage + ASCT: EFS 8.3 vs 2.0 mo (HR 0.40); 4-yr OS 54.6% vs 46.0%, HR 0.73 — the only 2L CAR-T OS win
TRANSFORM: EFS NR vs 2.4 mo, CR 74% vs 43%; OS HR 0.72, NS (crossover-adjusted HR 0.42)
Approved 2L (Jun 2022), incl. transplant-ineligible (PILOT ORR 80%, median age 74). Gr 3 CRS 1%
3L+ only. Lowest CR of the three (JULIET CR 40%)
PARMA (pre-R): ASCT 5-yr EFS 46% vs 12%. CORAL: R-ICE = R-DHAP (ORR ~63%); 3-yr EFS 20% if relapse <12 mo vs 45% if later
Standard for chemosensitive late relapse; 2–3 cycles then BEAM-ASCT
STARGLO: OS 25.5 vs 12.9 mo (HR 0.62) vs R-GemOx; enrollment largely ex-US
FDA CRL Jul 2025 — not approved in US (US applicability); still a handbook/NCCN option
EPCORE NHL-2 (single-arm): ORR 85%, CR 61%, median OS 21.6 mo
Not FDA-approved. EPCORE DLBCL-4 (epco + len vs R-GemOx) PFS positive, topline Jun 2026
GO29365: CR 40% vs 18%; OS 12.4 vs 4.7 mo — only 40 per arm
Approved 2019. Bendamustine impairs later T-cell collection — avoid before CAR-T apheresis
L-MIND single-arm: ORR 57.5%, CR 41%, mPFS 11.6 mo (5-yr) — best after 1 prior line
Still accelerated; CD19 — not before CD19 CAR-T is a real concern
ECHELON-3 vs placebo + R²: OS 13.8 vs 8.5 mo, HR 0.63 — benefit regardless of CD30
ZUMA-1 (axi-cel) ORR 82%, CR 54% · TRANSCEND (liso-cel) ORR 73%, CR 53% · JULIET (tisa-cel) ORR 52%, CR 40%
NP30179: CR 39% (35% post-CAR-T), fixed 12 cycles; median CR duration ~30 mo
EPCORE NHL-1: ORR 63%, CR 39%, SC, until progression. EPCORE DLBCL-1 vs R-GemOx/BR: PFS HR 0.74 (3.5 vs 3.0 mo) but OS HR 0.96 — US primary endpoint missed
Accelerated, ≥2 lines; confirmatory trial missed OS (EHA Jun 2026)
CD19-PBD ADC. LOTIS-2: ORR 48%, CR 24%. LOTIS-5 (lonca-R vs R-GemOx): PFS 6.1 vs 4.7 mo, HR 0.73; OS HR 0.96
Accelerated; confirmatory positive on PFS (Jun 2026). Edema/effusions, photosensitivity, GGT
blocks.footnote: Sequencing: CAR-T first when feasible — bispecifics work after CAR-T (glofit CR 35%), but CAR-T after CD19-directed therapy (tafasitamab, lonca) is less certain; confirm CD19 by IHC. Avoid bendamustine before apheresis.

blocks.heading: Choosing therapy at first relapse
items: Biopsy the relapse — confirm LBCL, check CD19 (before CD19-directed agents) and CD20 (lost in some after anti-CD20 therapy)
Timing is the strongest predictor. In CORAL, relapse <12 months after rituximab-containing therapy gave 3-yr EFS of only 20% with salvage + ASCT — this is why CAR-T replaced ASCT for early relapse
CAR-T eligibility is about organ function and performance status more than age — PILOT treated a median age of 74. Refer at relapse, not after failed salvage
Bridging: steroids, RT to bulky sites, pola-R ± bendamustine-free chemo; avoid bendamustine before apheresis
After CAR-T failure: bispecific (glofitamab fixed-duration, epcoritamab continuous), BV-R², loncastuximab, allo-HCT in fit chemosensitive patients, trial

blocks.heading: Transformed indolent lymphoma
items: Biopsy the fastest-growing / highest-SUV site (SUV discordance, rising LDH, B symptoms)
Anthracycline-naive → treat as de novo DLBCL (R-CHOP or Pola-R-CHP). Anthracycline-exposed → manage as R/R DLBCL
CAR-T and bispecific labels include DLBCL arising from follicular/indolent lymphoma. Richter (from CLL) is different — see the CLL card

pages.subtitle: Page 3 — regimen dosing, CRS/ICANS, toxicity and key trials

blocks.heading: Frontline dosing
rows: Rituximab 375 · cyclophosphamide 750 · doxorubicin 50 · vincristine 1.4 (cap 2 mg) — all d1; prednisone 100 mg d1–5 (handbook: 40 mg/m²). G-CSF if age ≥60
Polatuzumab 1.8 mg/kg replaces vincristine; R 375 · C 750 · H 50 d1; prednisone 100 mg d1–5. G-CSF required

R 375 d1; etoposide 50 + doxorubicin 10 + vincristine 0.4 /day CIV d1–4 (96 h); cyclophosphamide 750 d5; prednisone 60 BID d1–5 (NCI protocol; handbook lists 60/day); G-CSF from d6. CBC twice weekly: ANC nadir ≥500 → +20% (E, H, C); <500 on 3 checks or plt <25k → −20%
R 375 · C 400 · H 25 · V 1 mg flat d1; prednisone 40 d1–5
R 375 d1; gemcitabine 1000 d1+8; C 750 + V 1–1.4 d1; prednisolone 100 mg d1–5 — anthracycline-free
3–3.5 g/m² ×2–4 after R-CHOP; alkalinize urine pH >7, leucovorin rescue, levels to <0.1 µM; no third-spacing, no PPI/NSAID/TMP-SMX

blocks.heading: Deauville 5-point score
rows: Uptake > mediastinum but ≤ liver — usually adequate response
Moderately > liver · markedly > liver or new lesions — treatment failure
blocks.footnote: Response is reported this way in practice and in every trial cited. (The handbook itself specifies only PET/CT at completion, plus marrow biopsy if positive at diagnosis.)

blocks.heading: CRS and ICANS (ASTCT 2019)
rows: Hypotension without pressors and/or O₂ <6 L NC
One pressor and/or high-flow / face-mask O₂
ICE 0–2, wakes to touch; focal edema, seizure resolving
blocks.footnote: CRS: tocilizumab 8 mg/kg (max 800 mg) from grade 2 (earlier for CAR-T), add dexamethasone 10 mg q6h if refractory or grade 3+. ICANS: dexamethasone 10 mg q6h from grade 2; tocilizumab does not treat isolated ICANS (may worsen it); levetiracetam, neuro checks. Bispecific CRS clusters in cycle 1 after step-up doses.

blocks.heading: Salvage and R/R dosing
rows: R 375 d1; ifosfamide 5000 + mesna 5000 CIV 24 h d2; carboplatin AUC 5 (max 800 mg) d2; etoposide 100 d1–3
R 375 d1; cisplatin 100 CIV d1; cytarabine 2000 q12h ×2 d2 (1000 if >60; steroid eye drops); dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4. (R-DHAX: oxaliplatin 100)
R 375 d1; gemcitabine 1000 d1+8; dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4; cisplatin 75 d1 — outpatient, non-inferior to R-DHAP (LY.12)
Polatuzumab 1.8 mg/kg + R 375 d1; bendamustine 90 d1+2
Tafasitamab 12 mg/kg C1 d1, 4, 8, 15, 22 → C2–3 weekly → C4+ d1+15; lenalidomide 25 mg d1–21 ×12 cycles, then tafasitamab alone
0.15 mg/kg ×2 cycles, then 0.075 mg/kg; dexamethasone 4 mg BID d−1 to d1
BV 1.2 mg/kg (max 120 mg) + rituximab q3wk + lenalidomide 20 mg daily
Obinutuzumab 1000 mg C1D1 → 2.5 mg C1D8 (inpatient 24 h) → 10 mg C1D15 → 30 mg C2–12. Dexamethasone 20 mg IV before C1–3 doses

0.16 mg C1D1 → 0.8 mg C1D8 → 48 mg C1D15, D22; weekly C2–3, q2wk C4–9, q4wk C10+. Dexamethasone 15 mg (or prednisolone 100) on dosing day + 3 days after in C1. C1D15: outpatient monitoring allowed since Apr 2026
Axi-cel 2×10⁶/kg (max 2×10⁸) after flu 30 + cy 500 ×3 d · Liso-cel 90–110×10⁶ (2L) after flu 30 + cy 300 ×3 d · Tisa-cel 0.6–6×10⁸ after flu 25 + cy 250 ×3 d

blocks.heading: Toxicity and monitoring
items: Hepatitis B with every anti-CD20 (and bispecifics): HBsAg+ → entecavir/tenofovir; HBsAg− anti-HBc+ → prophylaxis (or monthly DNA); continue ≥12 months after the last dose
Cardiac: baseline echo; R-CHOP ×6 = doxorubicin 300 mg/m². Risk rises steeply past 400–450 mg/m² — dexrazoxane or anthracycline-free regimen when EF borderline
Tumor flare with bispecifics (and lenalidomide): painful node swelling, can compress airway/organs — steroids, antihistamine, hold
Infection: acyclovir + PJP prophylaxis with bispecifics, CAR-T, pola-BR, EPOCH; IVIG if IgG <400 with infections; CMV monitoring on bispecifics
CAR-T: REMS removed Jun 2025 — stay near center 2 weeks, no driving 2 weeks. Prolonged cytopenias; secondary T-cell malignancy boxed warning
Neuropathy from vincristine (cap 2 mg) and polatuzumab; TLS prophylaxis for bulky disease or high LDH

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: R-CHOP vs CHOP, age 60–80 — 10-yr OS 43.5% vs 27.6%
Pola-R-CHP: PFS HR 0.73 → 0.77 at 5 yr; OS HR 0.85, NS
Tafa-len-R-CHOP: PFS HR 0.75; more fatal AEs; OS immature
Limited stage: 4 cycles enough; PET-adapted, RT for iPET+ only
Liso-cel 2L EFS HR 0.35 (OS NS) / tisa-cel 2L negative
Epcoritamab vs chemo: PFS HR 0.74, OS HR 0.96 (NS)
PMBL in CMR: RT omission non-inferior
HD-MTX: no CNS-relapse reduction in 1,923 ultra-high-risk
CHOP ×3 + RT vs CHOP ×8 — early edge lost with time
PMBL EFS 93% without RT · MYC-rearranged 4-yr EFS 71%
ASCT beats salvage alone / R-ICE = R-DHAP; early relapse fares poorly
Pola-BR OS 12.4 vs 4.7 mo / tafa-len ORR 58%, CR 41%
Lonca ORR 48% / lonca-R vs R-GemOx PFS HR 0.73
R/R PMBL: pembro ORR 45% / nivo-BV ORR 73%
HIV: rituximab deaths at CD4 <50 / concurrent R-EPOCH CR 73%
